name: Shayan Chowdhury Arnob

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Jazz, Blues, Western rock (via band Bangla)
global_influences.evidence: The folk band Bangla, founded by Arnob in 1998, was explicitly noted as blending traditional Baul/Lalon material with Western flavours including jazz, blues and rock.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Shayan Chowdhury Arnob; Wikipedia Bangla (band)

global_influences.evidence: Arnob's formal training at Patha Bhavana and Kala Bhavana in Santiniketan (India) exposed him to a broader South Asian arts and music education that informed his cross-genre approach, distinct from the Dhaka rock-band pipeline.

local_adaptation_notes: Arnob's foundational move was forming the band Bangla (1998) explicitly to fuse Baul and Lalon folk traditions — the philosophical 'freedom' he found in Baul music being his stated inspiration — with Western musical idioms. His solo work builds on this synthesis with intimate, acoustic-leaning production, positioning him as a central figure in Bangladeshi folk fusion distinct from the rock-oriented mainstream lineage (James, LRB, Miles).
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period (1998–2000s): co-founded and led the folk-fusion band Bangla, blending Baul/Lalon vocal traditions with jazz, blues, and rock instrumentation. Solo breakthrough (2004–2005): 'She Je Boshe Ache' (for TV drama Offbeat) and debut solo album Chaina Bhabish (2005) established his solo folk-fusion voice. Consolidation period (2006–2009): Hok Kolorob and Doob deepened the folk-fusion aesthetic and built a devoted following, followed by a live international-tour album in 2009.
concert_culture_notes: Associated with intimate acoustic/live-band performance formats and international touring (noted international tour preceding the 2009 live album); performances often emphasize musicianship and folk instrumentation over large-scale rock production.
listener_community_notes: Central reference artist for the Folk & Folk Fusion genre in the BMEM framework alongside Coke Studio Bangla and Baul artists; attracts listeners overlapping with both traditional folk audiences and urban, cosmopolitan indie/alternative listeners.
